handoff: AC1–AC4 met and tested; blocking F1: checkout takes the claim and worktrees before fetching/unpacking the record, so a failed fetch or a corrupt record leaves the claim held with no run state and the next tick starts the story over (S2, B22), untested. Minor F2 (record_push shares the story unit's failures slot), F3 (restart skipped if unapplied receipts move the cursor); nits F4, F5.

findings.title: A failed record fetch or unpack leaves the claim held with no run state; the next tick starts the story over
findings.detail:
checkoutStory acquires the claim (line ~214) and checks out the story worktree (line ~234) before takeRecord fetches refs/norn/runs/<story> and unpacks it (line 242). When fetchRecords throws (network, retry text says 'the claim is held by you now') or unpackRecord returns !ok (failure 'record_corrupt', whose do_instead does not even say the claim is held), the command exits non-zero with the claim held, the worktree in place and no state.json in the machine dir. decideStory then sees claim 'mine', a worktree and no story unit state, and startStoryUnit emits start_unit with initialState — a fresh round at the workflow's first step with zero counters, the record silently lost (S2: never guess or start over; B22 'a handover loses nothing'). Under record.policy remote the next pushRecord leases on the sha fetchRecords just wrote into the local ref, so the fresh record is pushed on top of the real one. fetchRecords also force-updates the local ref before the record is validated. No test covers either failure path. Repro: hand over at review#2 as in takeover-record.test.ts, replace the remote ref with a commit whose tree holds an invalid state.json (or make the ref fetch fail), run checkout on B (non-zero), then B.tick(): expect no start_unit and the claim not held/the unit not restarted.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Fetch and validate the record (unpack into staging) before the claim and the worktrees, as the branchless path already fetches before the claim, and rename it into place only after the claim lands; or release the claim on a record failure. Add an integration test for a corrupt ref and for a failed ref fetch, each asserting the claim/run state afterwards and that the next tick does not start_unit.

findings.title: The record_push failure shares the story unit's single failures slot with its other act failures
findings.detail:
failures.json keeps one entry per unit key. recordPushFailure overwrites any pending failure of the story unit (e.g. a refused commit, whose Unblock item then disappears because actFailureItem returns null for record_push), and a later failure of another story-unit effect overwrites the record_push entry, so decide's hold in pushRecord (decide/story.ts:147) lapses, the push is retried with the same lease, refused again and overwrites the other failure: the two alternate tick by tick. The entry also stays forever if the claim moves elsewhere or the policy goes back to local (the item is hidden but the hold remains).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Keep the stale-lease fact apart from the unit's R4.3 slot (its own key or file), or at least never let one overwrite the other; clear it when the claim is no longer this checkout's.

findings.title: The restart keys on state.json's cursor, not the cursor after the record's unapplied receipts
findings.detail:
takeReceipt reads step/attempt from state.json; apply restarts only when the take's step/attempt equal the cursor when the take is applied. If the record carries unapplied receipts numbered before the take (an agent's done applied after the handoff push), they move the cursor first and the rewrite is silently ignored: the next step runs on the rewritten branch with no 'Why this attempt' (B24). Unlikely after a clean handoff, likelier after expiry/--force (B26).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Either restart whatever step the cursor is at when the take applies, or say in the output that the restart was skipped; a hand-built case would pin it.

findings.title: A branchless checkout fetches the record ref twice
findings.detail:
Line 212 calls fetchRecord to decide the story exists, then takeRecord (line 242) runs ls-remote + fetch again.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Fetch once before the claim and pass the result to takeRecord (which F1's fix would do anyway).

findings.title: The dropped `receipt: { pushed: true }` assertion is obsolete; its S12 counterpart is not asserted
findings.detail:
Under S12/D8 the take receipt is never committed or pushed, so the old assertion is rightly gone and the receipt is now read from B's machine dir. Nothing checks the opposite (the take receipt is not on the story branch, and under the default local policy no record push followed the take).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optionally assert the story branch tree has no runs/ take receipt.
